reply_text:
I found one 2023 candidate, and it is already in your recorded list. I saw it only in news coverage, never in Huang's own words or a transcript.

**The candidate (2023-11-29.toml).** At the New York Times DealBook Summit on 29 November 2023, Huang set a condition: if AGI means software that can pass tests in a way "fairly competitive" with human intelligence, then "within the next five years, you're going to see, obviously, AIs that can achieve those tests." I read this in CNBC's report. I didn't open a DealBook transcript or the video.

**Not confirmed: the 22 February earnings call (2023-02-22.toml).** I opened two transcripts of this call, from Motley Fool and AlphaStreet. Both pages were cut short before the part where Huang looks ahead. On AlphaStreet I could read only his look back: "we've accelerated and advanced AI processing by a million x over the last decade". Search snippets showed a forward line starting "Over the course of the next 10 years, I hope…" but I never read it on a page, so I haven't quoted it. YourStory reports that he expects "another one million times AI processing boost over the next ten years", but that is the paper's paraphrase, not his words. As written, it is also as much a claim about Nvidia's chips as about what AI will do. I didn't find the "gigantic breakthroughs" wording on any page I opened, so this recorded claim is still unchecked.

**Left out:**
- **NTU commencement, 27 May 2023.** Huang said "Within the next decade, our industry will replace over a trillion dollars of the world's traditional computers with new accelerated AI computers." That is a forecast about the computer business, so it stays out. His "I predict that 2023 will be as well" (a perfect year to graduate) isn't a prediction about AI.
- **Acquired podcast, October 2023.** The page I opened held only the first part of the transcript, which had no dated predictions. I can't say anything about the rest.

I used all 6 page openings and 9 of the 12 searches. I didn't spend the last 3, because I couldn't open any more pages to quote from.
